spec.title: A deep-RL policy (PPO) against holding
spec.question: Can a recurrent PPO policy beat buy-and-hold after costs?
spec.hypothesis: PPO earns a higher Sharpe than buy-and-hold across walk-forward folds.
spec.method: 9 walk-forward folds x 5 seeds x 9 tickers (405 runs), fees on every method, differences clustered by fold.
limitations: Run before the Lab existed: its criteria were not filed in advance, and it did not go through the reviewer.

review.summary: PPO trailed holding by -0.44 Sharpe (95% CI -0.70 to -0.17) and was ahead in 11% of folds. This is why HANSEI is a simple, explainable agent.

spec.title: Do the advisors predict returns?
spec.question: Across NSE large caps, do stocks an advisor likes outperform the ones it dislikes?
spec.hypothesis: Each advisor's liked-minus-disliked return spread is positive, 20 sessions ahead.
spec.method: 105 large caps, 2007 onward, tune and holdout splits, monthly-clustered confidence intervals.
limitations: Run before the Lab existed: its criteria were not filed in advance, and it did not go through the reviewer.

review.summary: 6 of 6 spreads have a 95% interval that includes zero. No advisor is a statistically reliable return signal; the volatility brake predicts bigger swings, not lower returns.

spec.title: Staying more invested (tolerance 0.2, floor 0.5)
spec.question: Would a rule that cuts exposure later, and never below half, beat the live rule?
spec.hypothesis: A more-invested rule keeps most of the drawdown protection and earns more.
spec.method: 12 tolerance/floor settings swept on 2007-2019 with a rule fixed in advance (best Tune 2007-2019 CAGR with drawdown at least 5% smaller than holding's); the chosen setting checked once on 2020 onward.
limitations: Run before the Lab existed: its criteria were not filed in advance, and it did not go through the reviewer.

review.summary: On 2020 onward it beat holding by +1.22% a year against the live rule's +1.03%, with a lower Sharpe edge (+0.15 vs +0.23). A later check on the falling Jul 2024 onward window had it behind the live rule. Not switched on.

spec.title: Does reading the news help?
spec.question: Does adding scored headlines improve the agent, on news the scoring model could not have seen in training?
spec.hypothesis: With news, HANSEI earns more than without it over Jul 2024 onward.
spec.method: The agent replayed with and without archived, model-scored headlines over the same days; the news view also scored on its own.
limitations: Run before the Lab existed: its criteria were not filed in advance, and it did not go through the reviewer.

review.summary: News added +0.44% a year, with a 65% chance of being better than no news: noise. On its own the news view was right 46% of the time over 1,733 opinions. It stays live because it is cheap and its live record is short.

spec.title: An earnings-surprise advisor
spec.question: Should a fifth advisor react to results that beat or miss estimates?
spec.hypothesis: Adding it raises returns against the four-advisor rule in tune and holdout.
spec.method: 402 results announcements for the five stocks; the hold period chosen on 2007-2019, then checked on 2020 onward across the settings grid.
limitations: Run before the Lab existed: its criteria were not filed in advance, and it did not go through the reviewer.

review.summary: It lowered 2007-2019 returns by -0.32% a year and helped in 5 of 9 holdout settings. Small cross-sectional edges do not survive a hold-by-default design. Not added.

spec.title: The live rule against holding
spec.question: Does the rule HANSEI trades with today beat simply holding the five stocks?
spec.hypothesis: It falls less than holding and has a higher Sharpe, in both spans. It is not expected to earn more.
spec.method: The real brain and memory replayed day by day on the frozen price snapshot: decide after each close, fill at the next open, pay NSE costs, idle cash in a liquid fund. Two spans: 2007-2019 (the years the rule was tuned on) and 2020 onward (the years it was not).
limitations: Five stocks chosen because the owner already held them; they move together.
The news advisor is silent in this replay: there is no scored news history before 2012.
The replay trades rupee amounts; the live ₹10,000 book trades whole shares and is less invested.
The holdout years (2020 onward) have been looked at before, during earlier tuning.

spec.title: Where the edge comes from
spec.question: Under which market conditions does HANSEI beat holding, and under which does it lag?
spec.hypothesis: It beats holding while the five-stock basket is in a downtrend and lags while it is in an uptrend, in both spans.
spec.method: The real brain and memory replayed day by day on the frozen price snapshot: decide after each close, fill at the next open, pay NSE costs, idle cash in a liquid fund. Two spans: 2007-2019 (the years the rule was tuned on) and 2020 onward (the years it was not). Each session is labelled from the previous close: is the equal-weight basket above where it was 126 sessions ago (up or down), and is its 20-session volatility above its one-year median (choppy or calm). Returns are annualised within each label.
limitations: Five stocks chosen because the owner already held them; they move together.
The news advisor is silent in this replay: there is no scored news history before 2012.
The replay trades rupee amounts; the live ₹10,000 book trades whole shares and is less invested.
The holdout years (2020 onward) have been looked at before, during earlier tuning.
Descriptive: it splits one run by condition and has no bootstrap. Labels use the five stocks themselves, not the wider market.
